# H14 experimental normalized point protocol v1
This frozen experimental protocol is separate from production contracts. The only
accepted model output is a JSON object with exactly `point`, an array of exactly two
integers in 0..1000. Whitespace is allowed. Reuse the previously calibrated explicit
wrapper contract: either bare JSON or one exact `\`\`\`json` opening followed by
a newline and JSON, then a newline and `\`\`\`` closing. This compatibility
choice predates all H14 inference. Other fences, commentary, surrounding junk,
duplicate keys, floats, booleans, null, nonfinite constants and additional keys fail closed.
Maximum output text is 4096 characters. Invalid output causes no fixture event.
For an RGB image W by H (integer dimensions 1..4096), each axis maps with
`min(size - 1, floor(coordinate * size / 1000))`. Zero maps to the first pixel;
1000 maps to the last pixel. Rectangles are `[left, top, right, bottom)` in image
pixels. Screen origins, window borders, CSS coordinates and logical DPI units are
absent. DPI metadata does not rescale the frame; no screenshot resize/crop is
performed by the scorer. The processor may internally resize visual input, but
the model's requested output frame remains the original image. Never map these
points directly to a native display without a separately qualified adapter.
The prompt contains only the user's goal and the protocol instruction. The model
receives the rendered screenshot, not target IDs, hit boxes or expected state.
A valid point creates at most one selection event in an original one-click
synthetic fixture. The independent scorer checks the selection against private
CPU implementation is experimental. No model result or native qualification is
implied by the synthetic oracle/negative controls. The immutable manifest and its
externally recorded SHA-256 establish a prospective source/task/prompt freeze.
Never re-freeze this version or tune prompts after observing heldout inference;
repairs after evaluation require a new declared experiment and prospective tasks.
Before inference, author/freeze explicitly from the repository root:
Existing pre-inference freezes require `--replace-pre-inference` and a fresh
recorded hash. Review/qualification evidence remains separate and parent-owned.
The freeze captures source byte hashes, including this runner and protocol, not
just a dataset count. Source line ending changes invalidate it.
On an authorized free remote Linux CUDA allocation only, inspect and install the
exact versions in `heldout_runner.VERSIONS`: torch 2.11.0 (CUDA wheel suffix is
recorded), transformers 5.16.1, Pillow 11.3.0. Use an actual RAQM-enabled Pillow

# H14: frozen coordinate protocol and prospective bilingual held-out GUI evaluation

Status: in progress. Depends on: H5 diagnostic and H3 infrastructure built in this run. Surfaces: new experimental protocol/heldout modules, frozen evaluation specifications, remote runner and dedicated tests/docs. Production contracts remain separate.

Use one shared pinned Qwen3-VL-2B unchanged model first. Freeze an explicit normalized 0..1000 protocol, half-open target rectangles, image-pixel/DPI assumptions, deterministic mapping and failure behavior. Reject malformed/nonfinite/bool/extra/duplicate coordinate outputs. No execution authority or completion receipt from the model.

Generate 64 prospective GUI task instances, balanced English/Arabic, across eight original families unlike the prior four-button diagnostic and the existing training families. Vary layouts/dimensions/targets/distractors and task semantics; disclose family dependence. No training or test-set prompt tuning. Freeze specifications and protocol hashes before evaluating; remote-render Arabic only with actual RAQM and a declared font, freeze resulting images before inference. Keep expected targets/private state out of model inputs. Simulated executable environments may report complete-task success only for their declared fixture scope, never native Windows/browser task qualification.
- [ ] Strict protocol specification and deterministic failure/edge/DPI tests.
- [ ] Frozen source manifest with 64 instances, eight independent families, original rights and balanced languages; no old calibration task/image reuse.

- [ ] Remote runner verifies hashes, renders all inputs before loading model, records actual provenance/latency/allocated and device residency measures, schema validity, hit/wrong-target/miss rates and English/Arabic intervals.
- [ ] Negative providers demonstrate scorer rejects wrong targets, invalid outputs and false completion; no model sees expected target/terminal state.
- [ ] Relevant tests and full CPU suite; genuine Jev/Graft and independent PStack delta review.
- [ ] Actual free-GPU evaluation when available, source/dataset frozen before inference; no fabricated score on allocation failure.

Assumptions: eight authored families are a narrow reproducible GUI fixture sample, not a population-representative desktop benchmark. Wilson intervals are descriptive; provide family-level summaries and clearly label correlation. GPU allocation is external; CPU implementation/reviews proceed regardless. No paid activation or local weights.
